All three open PRs touch Linux clipboard/middle-click paste but they're __not really duplicates__ — each addresses a diiferent issue with pasting.

## Summary Table

| PR                                                         | Title                                                                              | Problem                                                                                                         | Approach                                                                                                                            | Files                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| [#16379](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16379) | fix(tui): support middle-click paste from X11 primary selection                    | Middle-clicking **into** opencode's prompt does nothing                                                         | On `MouseButton.MIDDLE`, call new `Clipboard.readPrimary()` and insert text                                                         | `clipboard.ts`, `prompt/index.tsx`      |
| [#6370](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/6370)   | fix: enable primary clipboard copy for Wayland/X11 to fix Linux middle-click paste | Text **copied from** opencode doesn't populate the primary selection, so other apps can't middle-click paste it | On copy, optionally also write to the primary clipboard via `--primary` flag; opt-in via `clipboard.linux.enablePrimaryCopy` config | `clipboard.ts`, `config.ts`             |
| [#10332](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/10332) | feat(opencode): add linux clipboard toast warnings                                 | Clipboard operations silently fail when `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` are not installed                              | Return a `CopyResult` with a notice/warning and show toasts in the TUI                                                              | `clipboard.ts`, multiple TUI call sites |

## Why They Are Complementary

- **#16379** fixes the **read/paste** direction: opencode reads the primary selection on middle-click so users can paste text selected in another app.
- **#6370** fixes the **write/copy** direction: opencode writes to the primary selection on copy so other apps can middle-click paste content from opencode.
- **#10332** is orthogonal: it improves feedback when clipboard tools are missing, regardless of which direction data is flowing.

As of today, all three can be merged independently and without conflict.

> For anyone having the same issue there is a workaround .
> 
> Download lombok.jar : https://projectlombok.org/downloads/lombok.jar
> 
> {
>   "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
>   "lsp": {
>     "jdtls": {
>       "disabled": true
>     },
>     "jdtls-lombok": {
>       "command": [
>         "{env:HOME}/.local/share/opencode/bin/jdtls/bin/jdtls",
>         "--jvm-arg=-javaagent:{env:HOME}/dev-tools/jars/lombok.jar",
>         "-configuration",
>         "{env:HOME}/.local/share/opencode/bin/jdtls/config_linux",
>         "-data",
>         "/tmp/opencode-jdtls-data"
>       ],
>       "extensions": [
>         ".java"
>       ]
>     }
>   }
> }
> It should also be possible to use your own version of jdtls by using the one from neovim, vscode, eclipse or building it from source : https://github.com/eclipse-jdtls/eclipse.jdt.ls.
